[...] - A123: a tone whose main contour is level, starting at low pitch [...] the author notates it as [22] [...] - A4: [...] [55] [...] - B123: [...] [35] [...] - B4: [...] [32] [...] - C123: this tone has a falling contour starting from mid pitch. new_statements.relation_note: Full segmental inventory (20 onsets incl. implosives ɓ ɗ, no palatalized Cj- clusters; 9 codas incl. -ʔ; 16 vowel phones with length contrast) and the complete tone box; tone values said to be close to Tai Dam and Tai Dón. Silent on stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Tày Sa Pa (Tày Mường Bo) is a lexical tone language with a Southwestern-Tai-type split system: six tones on smooth syllables — A123 [22] (variants 221, 21), A4 [55], B123 [35], B4 [32] (variant 332), C123 creaky [3̰1] (variant 31̰2), C4 [52] — and on checked syllables DS123 [55]~[45], DL123 [35] before -p -t -k but [52] before -ʔ, DS4/DL4 [32] (= B4). Every syllable carries a tone; nothing is said about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: DL123 has two coda-conditioned values ([35] with -p/-t/-k, [52] with -ʔ); allotonic variants listed for A123, B4, C123, DS123; vowel length contrast flagged as needing more study
new_statements.identity_note: The paper states explicitly that Tày Mường Bo = Tày Sa Pa = Glottolog tays1238 ('Tày Mường Bo hay còn được biết đến với tên gọi là Tày Sa Pa'; cites glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/tays1238 and Edmondson's Borderlands project as the origin of the name 'Tày Sa Pa'); speakers are the Tày of Bản Hồ, Liên Minh and Mường Bo communes, Sa Pa town, Lào Cai (~2,500 people in 2009); classified Southwestern Tai, lacking the /Cj-/ palatalized onsets of Northeastern (Central Tai) Tày; compared with Tai Dam / Tai Dón. Not Pa Dí [pdi].

sources.citation: Pittayaporn, Pittayawat. 2009. The phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University, Ithaca. xix+417 pp. (Sapa = dialect no. 48 in the 68-dialect sample; data from the author's unpublished fieldnote 'Tay of Sapa' (Pittayaporn 2007e), fieldwork winter 2008.)
sources.note: Nothing about stress in Sapa. Sapa appears only as a comparative data point: p. 20 (fieldwork on 'the Tai dialects of Sapa, Bao Yen, and Cao Bang'), p. 302 ('This variety is extremely similar to subgroup Q [= SWT], but did not go through the change from *kr- to *ʰr-'), p. 309, p. 319 (dialect list, source 'Pittayaporn (2007e)'), plus the lexical appendix. The only stress discussion is the general foot typology (Hayes 1995) and sesquisyllabic-vs-monosyllabic prosodic-word argument for Proto-Tai (ch. 2), not a statement about Sapa.
